Subject: Staggered renewal notice / termination-for-convenience clarity for Order Form

Sophie — following up from our call this morning. Thanks again for walking through the pilot timing. Before legal signs off we need to align on a few narrow points in the MSA/order form related to term, auto-renew, and termination for convenience. Copying Soojin and Karthik so we can get a clean redline and a short rationale back to Novus.

High level asks from Novus we heard:
- Novus wants a single auto-renew clause that applies globally but requests a shorter notice window (30 days) to opt out.
- They asked to preserve a unilateral "termination for convenience" right on their side with a 30-day notice and no termination fees.
- They also want an explicit data export delay (30 days post-termination) and a handoff SLA.

Our proposed starting points (what we prefer):
- Auto-renew by default but with a 60-day notice for enterprise SKUs (gives us runway for renewal ops).
- Termination for convenience remains mutual, not unilateral; if exercised, include a 60-day notice and transition support obligations tied to invoice credits for unused committed capacity.
- Data export window/hand-off: 45 days with read-only access to exported KV cache; standard fees for extraordinary data egress only.

Soojin — can you please advise on legal risk/standard language we should circulate? Karthik — if we need to trade on price or credits to compress the notice window, what levers are you willing to authorize?

Attachments: I attached the current Order Form draft for reference.

Thanks,
Hannah

Hannah / team — forwarding our counsel note. Key rationale from our side:
- Novus operates in a regulated payments environment; they need the flexibility in the pilot year to wind down or shift vendors quickly if their integrations expose risk. A 30-day convenience termination for the first 12 months is a reasonable commercial ask in that context.
- Shorter auto-renew notice reduces the chance of inadvertent auto-renewal for small business customers Novus manages.
- Data export: Novus cannot accept extended delays beyond 30 days for export due to reconciliation deadlines with partners.

We are open to limited transition assistance language (e.g., a short run-rate credit for unused months) in lieu of ongoing support obligations. See redline for proposed language.

-Michael

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Staggered renewal notice / termination-for-convenience clarity for Order Form

Hannah / Karthik — reviewed Novus's redline and counsel note. My read and proposed compromise below.

Summary of risk:
- Unilateral 30-day termination for Novus in the first 12 months increases churn and revenue recognition complexity. It also creates potential capacity and deprovisioning load without recovery unless credit mechanics are clear.
- A blanket 30-day auto-renew notice across all SKUs increases our operational risk during renewal season.

Proposed compromise language (high level):
1) Auto-renew: Keep auto-renew, but split by SKU tier. Enterprise (committed/reserved) products require 60 days' notice; Standard (pay-as-you-go/pilot) will accept 30 days. We can add a short sentence allowing Novus to opt-in to 30-day for any SKU if they pay a nominal shorter-notice fee (e.g., 10% of monthly commit for 60-day compression).

2) Termination for convenience: Allow Novus a one-time unilateral termination for convenience during the initial 12-month pilot, but require 60 days' notice and a modest termination processing fee (pro-rated credits for unused months plus a 10% administrative fee). Mutual termination thereafter. Rationale: limits churn risk while offering flexibility they need.

3) Data export / handoff: 30 days read-only export window is acceptable for standard exports. For large dataset export or custom migration assistance, standard SOWs and egress fees apply. Add explicit language guaranteeing read-only access during the export window.

4) Operational protections: Add an express obligation for Novus to provide a migration runbook 14 days prior to the effective termination date to avoid ad hoc support burdens.

If you want, I can prepare a short negotiated redline that implements the above and includes fallback language if Novus insists on unilateral 30-day termination without fee (we should decline that).

Karthik — from commercial, we should decide the maximum discount / credit you are comfortable offering in exchange for shortening notice or waiving fees. Please confirm a hard cap so I can put numbers in the redline.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Novus negotiation plan — next steps

Karthik / Lauren — per Soojin's advice above, here's my proposed negotiation posture to send to Novus:

- Agree to tiered notice window: 30 days for pilot/standard; 60 days for enterprise/reserved. Offer a one-time option to compress to 30 for enterprise at a nominal short-notice fee (we can discuss exact percent).
- Offer a one-time unilateral termination-for-convenience for the initial 12 months, but require 60 days' notice + pro-rated credit and a 10% admin charge. No unilateral termination without fee.
- Confirm 30-day read-only export window; we will reserve right to charge for extraordinary egress and for custom migration services. Require Novus to provide migration runbook 14 days before termination effective date.

Ask: Karthik — can you authorize up to a 15% short-notice fee for compression and up to a 25% pro-rated credit cap for unused committed months (plus the 10% admin charge)? If yes, I will send the revised redline and a brief note explaining the trade (flexibility in return for limited financial recovery).

Lauren — please draft a one-paragraph negotiation note I can include in the email to Sophie that frames this as a cooperative compromise with clear operational guardrails. Once Karthik confirms, Soojin will insert the language and I will send to Novus.

Thanks,
Hannah
